plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. It is widely grown in gardens and commercial fields for its essential oil, and it attracts bees and butterflies in large numbers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, coarse stem and a showy flower head made of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disk of tiny florets. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early July to September in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Native to North America; grown across the Great Plains, Ukraine, Russia, southern France, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Young sunflowers follow the sun in a movement called heliotropism, but mature blooms stop moving and generally face east.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial whose large, round leaves rise above the water and whose showy, fragrant flowers open on tall stalks. Its water-repellent leaves stay clean, and its seed pods resemble shower heads.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to September in temperate Asia; peak in July
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands of India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and southeastern Russia; cultivated worldwide in water gardens
plants.funFact: Lotus flowers can regulate their own temperature, staying around 30-35°C even when the surrounding air is much cooler, which helps attract pollinating beetles.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the genus, made up of showy pink bracts surrounding a central cone of small flowers. It thrives in the nutrient-poor soils of the fynbos.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere late autumn to spring, with peak flowering from about May to September
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of the southwestern and southern Cape in South Africa; its national flower
plants.funFact: Proteas are an ancient lineage that predates the breakup of Gondwana and is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change form.
